title: Promotion of Collaborative Tripartism through National Education Curriculum
what_it_is: Promotion of Collaborative Tripartism through National Education Curriculum

sections.label: Tripartism taught through school subjects
sections.summary: Students learn about tripartism through History and Economics, covering mediation, stability, foreign investment and economic policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: While it is not specifically taught in a module labelled "tripartism", students do learn about it in a number of ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: For example, through History, secondary school students learn how the Labour Movement activity in the 1950s created the need for mediation to maintain peaceful relations between workers and employers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Junior college History students study strategies adopted by Southeast Asian countries to pursue development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: They may explore the case study of Singapore and learn how tripartism contributed to stability which attracted foreign investment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: In Economics, the study of national economic policies, like economic restructuring, wage level management, labour productivity and mobility, allow for the discussion of the roles played by employers, employees and the Government in maintaining a conducive economic climate.

sections.label: MOE curriculum review and Temasek Polytechnic programme
sections.summary: MOE reviews curriculum and a Temasek Polytechnic programme lets students experience agencies contributing to tripartism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: MOE regularly reviews our curriculum to better engage our students, and we will continue to help them learn how societies build consensus, in the same way that tripartism builds consensus and collaboration between unions, employers and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, Madam, if I can give an example, there is a programme between Temasek Polytechnic and the Singapore National Employers Federation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Through this, the students will have experience in the Ministry of Manpower, Industrial Arbitration Court, National Trades Union Congress, the Workplace Safety and Health Council, and the Tripartite Alliance for Fair Employment Practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, through a variety of processes and interactions, the students can learn about the different agencies, offices and activities that contribute towards the outcome of tripartism.
